subject: Hosted API quickstart vs Dedicated/Private — post-demo practicals & ops questions
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Cole <andrew@bluemerchant.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API quickstart vs Dedicated/Private — post-demo practicals & ops questions

Hi Andrew —

Thanks again for your time today — appreciated the demo session and the candid discussion about where BlueMerchant is headed. Quick recap and a few operational questions so we can scope a clean pilot: 

What we heard:
- Priority is fast time-to-value (NLP features in checkout & order triage) — low-latency responses matter for UX.
- Data residency: some PII must stay within your US controls, but it's acceptable for comms metadata to flow off-prem.
- Expected load (rough): peak ~120 reqs/s during promos, average ~20 reqs/s; typical request is ~150 tokens in, ~50 tokens out.

Our recommended immediate path (short answer): try a Hosted API pilot so you can validate output and latency without infra setup; if sustained peak throughput or strict VPC-only rules require it, we can map to Dedicated or Private later.

Operational questions for your team (can you confirm):
1) Is the traffic profile above accurate for pilot scope? please provide peak RPS and avg tokens per request if you have telemetry.
2) Do you require a dedicated VPC for any pilot traffic, or is a hosted demonstration acceptable with contract-level controls?
3) For the pilot, what SLOs do you need for 99th-pct latency (e.g., <200ms for short responses)?
4) Will you need audit logs / long-term retention during pilot (we can enable 90-day retention by request)?

Next steps I suggest:
- If you confirm traffic, Monica (cc'd) will propose a lightweight quickstart config (endpoints, rate limits, sample batching) and a short test plan you can run in 48–72 hours.
- We’ll attach a one-page quickstart playbook and a sample YAML config for your engs to review.

If Hosted looks good, conversion to Dedicated is a straight mapping of throughput + burst profile; we’ll include that in the quickstart doc so you have clarity on when to switch.

Thanks — I’ll wait for the traffic + residency confirmation and any other constraints.

—Aditya

Thanks Aditya — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

Traffic profile (rough, derived from current feature toggles):
- Baseline avg: 15–25 reqs/s globally (US peak is about 60% of global).
- Promo peak: up to ~140 reqs/s for short bursts (3–6 minutes).
- Tokens: avg input ~140 tokens, avg output ~60 tokens; 95th tokens ~400 for edge-case analytics requests.

Residency: pilot can run on hosted API as long as we can get contract language stating that input content will not be used to train models, and we can enable customer-controlled keying (KMS) for production later. We cannot accept traffic routing through third-country regions for PII — US-only is preferred.

SLOs: 99th percentile latency target <300ms for the main checkout intent (we can tolerate slower responses for long analytics queries).

Audit logs: yes, we’ll need request/response metadata for 30 days during the pilot.

We’re fine to start with hosted; please have Monica propose the rate-limited endpoints and any suggested batching. Also attach any sample payloads for our engs to stress.

—Andrew

Hi all —

Thanks — pulling together a short technical quickstart and the requested artifacts. Summary and recommended path below, plus attached YAML sample.

Recommendation (short): start with Hosted API pilot using the configuration below. Rationale: rapid onboarding, minimal infra changes, and we can control rate-limits and KMS options. If sustained peak >120–140 reqs/s with long-tail tokens, we typically recommend Dedicated for predictable latency and predictable marginal cost. Private (VPC/on-prem) is only recommended if you have regulatory or network egress constraints that block hosted traffic entirely.

Proposed quickstart config (Pilot):
- Duration: 2 weeks
- Endpoints: POST /v1/generate (timeout 5s), POST /v1/analytics (timeout 30s)
- Pilot throttles: global 150 rps burstable, per-key 80 rps baseline, 10 reqs/s concurrency limit per connection
- Token limits: 600 tokens/request hard limit (recommended), suggested batch size 8 for analytics route
- SLOs: target p50 80–120ms, p95 <200ms, p99 <320ms for /v1/generate under pilot profile
- Audit logs: enable 30-day request metadata export (JSONL to S3 or Drive link)
- KMS: recommend bringing your own key for production; pilot can use redwood-managed keys with contract confirmation

Attachments included: BM_QS_sample_config.yaml (sample env + rate-limits + curl), redwood-quickstart-playbook.pdf (1p).

Test plan (high-level):
1) Week 0: exchange API keys and enable 30-day metadata retention.
2) Day 1: smoke tests with 100 simulated concurrent users (50 rps).
3) Day 2–3: ramp to 80 rps sustained, validate p95/p99.
4) Day 4: brief burst test to 150 rps for 6 minutes; validate fallback and throttling behavior.
5) Exit: if p99 < 320ms and functionality validated, discuss Dedicated sizing + contract.

Questions for BlueMerchant to confirm:
- Are the per-key throttle numbers acceptable?
- Any objection to redwood-managed keys for pilot? (we can swap to BYOK before prod)

Andrew / eng-team: I attached the YAML and a single curl example in the playbook. Let me know a good time this week for a 30-minute run-through with your infra lead and I’ll schedule.

—Monica
